clue.text: Bath companion takes car oil, oddly enough, for soap

indicators.note: oddly enough says the letters taken together turn up in a strange new order

parts.note: a CB is a Companion of the Order of the Bath, a British honour

explanation.surface: A bather's companion brings along some car oil instead of soap, which is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bath companion' looks like a sponge or a towel, but it is CB, the honour; 'takes' joins it to CAR OIL and 'oddly enough' shuffles the whole pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbolic is a strong-smelling disinfectant soap made with phenol.

clue.text: Curse them breaking three articles

indicators.note: breaking says the word them splits the run of articles open from inside

parts.note: the articles an, a and a, set side by side
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone curses a group while chopping up three newspaper articles.
explanation.walkthrough: THEM goes between AN A and the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal ecclesiastical damnation, a solemn malediction.

clue.text: The colours of the beaten side ?

definitions.text: The colours of the beaten side ?

parts.words: The colours of the beaten side
parts.note: a beaten team's colours read as the shades of bruising on someone who has been thrashed

explanation.walkthrough: Sports teams wear colours; the 'side' that is beaten is a body bruised all over.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone covered in bruises after a beating is described with these two dark shades.

clue.text: It's the physical bond that makes us cry about the returning soldier

indicators.note: about says the wail is wrapped around the soldier

parts.note: to lament is to cry or wail in grief

indicators.note: returning means the soldier's letters are read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A bond so physical it makes us weep over a soldier coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's the' and 'that makes us' are link words; 'returning' turns the soldier round before 'about' wraps the cry around him.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is the tough band of tissue that binds bones together in the body.

clue.text: Street worker found at last?

parts.note: one who lays the stones of a street, and also a craftsman who works at a shoemaker's last

explanation.walkthrough: A last is the foot-shaped block a shoemaker works on; 'at last' is not 'finally'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a mender of shoes, who uses a last, and one who paves roads with rounded stones.

clue.text: But too much in our diet makes us flabby

definitions.text: But too much in our diet makes us flabby

parts.words: But too much in our diet makes us flabby
parts.note: a carbohydrate food essential in moderation, but fattening in excess; the word also names what stiffens a shirt, the opposite of flabby

explanation.walkthrough: The irony: the stuff that stiffens collars makes people go soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Starchy carbohydrates such as bread and potatoes are blamed for weight gain, while laundry stiffener makes cloth firm.

clue.text: She'll never get up in the charts

definitions.text: She'll never get up in the charts

parts.words: She'll never get up in the charts
parts.note: a record that does not climb the charts is not a hit, so the singer is the opposite of a hit; the title also suits a young unmarried woman

explanation.definitionFit: A failure as opposed to a hit is this word, which is also the title for an unmarried young woman.

clue.text: Removes perfume from the godowns ?

definitions.meaning: takes the smell away from something
goings down, downward slopes or drops

explanation.definitionFit: Split as de-scents it means takes away the fragrance; read whole it means downward movements or slopes.

clue.text: Wishful mood of one away from Grantchester

definitions.text: Wishful mood of one away from Grantchester

parts.words: Wishful mood of one away from Grantchester
parts.note: the grammatical mood of wishing, as in Rupert Brooke's homesick poem written in Berlin longing for the village near Cambridge

explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Brooke wrote 'The Old Vicarage, Grantchester' while abroad, wishing he were back in the Cambridgeshire village.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the mood expressing a wish, as in Greek, carries this name.

clue.text: State of duplication round the bend

indicators.note: of duplication says the state's abbreviation is written twice over

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for Georgia, a US state

explanation.surface: A state of doubled vision while driving round a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' is not a condition but Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are informal for crazy or mad.

clue.text: In which the performers need room to bow

definitions.text: In which the performers need room to bow

parts.words: In which the performers need room to bow
parts.note: a room is a chamber, and bowing is what string players do, so this is the small-ensemble playing meant for a room

explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' looks like taking a bow at the end; it is drawing a bow across strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Works for small instrumental groups were written to be played in a private room rather than a hall.

clue.text: Quality of the rockers but not of the rock

definitions.text: Quality of the rockers but not of the rock

parts.words: Quality of the rockers but not of the rock
parts.note: things that rock to and fro wobble, whereas a rock is firm and stable

explanation.definitionFit: Wobbliness belongs to what sways, not to a solid boulder.

clue.text: Arch witch

parts.note: the chief witch, queen of witches in Macbeth and Greek goddess of witchcraft

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of sorcery appears as the leader of the witches in Shakespeare's Macbeth.

clue.text: Worshipper of great Diana

parts.note: the crowd's cry in Acts 19, Great is Diana of the people of that city

explanation.walkthrough: The Bible's Acts 19:28 has the citizens of Ephesus crying 'Great is Diana'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Acts the citizens of Ephesus shout praise of their goddess Diana, whose temple stood there.

clue.text: Charge a man that has an appointment

parts.note: man taken as written
a date is an appointment to meet

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of something just because he has a date.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official charge or commission to act.

clue.text: Raisin wine

definitions.meaning: a sweet fortified drink made from muscat grapes

explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a raisin from the muscat vine and the sweet dessert drink made from that grape.

clue.text: Things grammatical

parts.note: things in general, and in grammar the nouns that receive a verb's action

explanation.definitionFit: The word means things in everyday speech and the receivers of a verb's action in grammar.

clue.text: Obtain some fortification from the Cabin Bar

indicators.note: from says the fortification is to be made out of the letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone retrieves a defensive structure from a pub in a hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obtain some ... from' suggests a hidden word, but the letters of CABIN BAR are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbican is an outer defensive tower guarding a castle gate.

clue.text: Motorist's obstruction-on a ring road ?

parts.note: a bell tolls when it rings
gate is a northern English and Scots word for a street or way

explanation.surface: A driver is held up by roadworks on a ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring road' looks like one thing, a bypass; it is two pieces. Gate meaning street survives in northern place names.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier where drivers must pay before passing holds up traffic.

clue.text: In search of a solution to the crime?

definitions.text: In search of a solution to the crime?

parts.words: In search of a solution to the crime
parts.note: a coroner's official inquiry into a death, which is literally being in pursuit of an answer

explanation.definitionFit: A judicial inquiry into a suspicious death seeks the cause, and can be read as being on a quest.

clue.text: A broth of a boy ? On the contrary!

definitions.text: A broth of a boy ? On the contrary!

parts.words: A broth of a boy ? On the contrary
parts.note: a broth of a boy is Irish for a fine lad, so the opposite is an Irish rascal or good-for-nothing

explanation.walkthrough: 'A broth of a boy' is an Irish expression of praise; the clue wants its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish word for a scamp or worthless fellow, the reverse of a splendid young man.

clue.text: Edward took it upon himself and did the necessary paper-work

indicators.note: upon in a down clue means the word it sits on top of the next piece

parts.note: Ed is short for Edward
taken as written
himself refers back to Edward, so ED again

explanation.surface: Edward took on the job alone and handled the paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took it upon himself' looks like an idiom for volunteering; in a down clue 'upon' stacks it above Edward's second appearance, 'himself'.
explanation.definitionFit: Editing is preparing text for publication, a newspaper's paperwork.

clue.text: A problem to shoot full of holes

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a puzzling question and to perforate thoroughly, as with gunfire.

clue.text: Was Madame de Pompadour as old as she implied ?

definitions.text: Was Madame de Pompadour as old as she implied ?

parts.words: Was Madame de Pompadour as old as she implied
parts.note: her famous remark after us the deluge implies she came before the Flood

explanation.walkthrough: Madame de Pompadour, mistress of Louis XV, is credited with 'Après nous le déluge', after us the deluge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word literally means from before the Flood, so very old-fashioned.

clue.text: Waggish conclusion

parts.note: waggish read as able to wag, and a conclusion as the end, so the rear end of a dog

explanation.definitionFit: The end of an animal is the part that wags.

clue.text: Dash away from the landlord

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone races off to escape the landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash away' reads as fleeing; 'Dash' alone is the definition, and the answer runs across 'thE LANdlord'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is flair and vigour, the same spirit as dash.

clue.text: They describe these disturbances round the mine

indicators.note: round says the scrambled letters surround the mine
disturbances says the letters of these are stirred up

parts.note: a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: Reports describe unrest around a colliery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbances' makes EHETS from 'these'; 'round' sets that around the mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive words or phrases attached to a name are adjectives of description.

clue.text: Element of filament

parts.note: the metal used for the thin glowing wire in a light bulb

explanation.definitionFit: This metallic chemical element, symbol W, makes the glowing wire in incandescent bulbs.
